business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 7 business descriptions
business_model.claim: CompX makes engineered components in two product lines: cabinet locks and other locking mechanisms (Security Products), and wake enhancement systems, stainless steel exhaust, gauges, throttles and trim tabs for recreational marine and other industries (Marine Components).
quotes: Our Security Products segment manufactures mechanical and electrical cabinet locks and other locking mechanisms

We also manufacture wake enhancement systems, stainless steel exhaust systems, gauges, throttle controls, trim tabs and related hardware and accessories for the recreational marine and other industries

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q income statement and the segment table in 10-Q MD&A
business_model.claim: Security Products is the larger segment by sales. In the first nine months of 2026, consolidated net sales were $128,174, of which Security Products was $94,921 and Marine Components $33,253 (all tables in thousands).

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q segment table (margins printed in percent columns)
business_model.claim: Security Products also earns most of the segment operating income. In the first nine months of 2026 it earned $20,620 against $7,251 for Marine Components (table in thousands), and its operating margin was 21.7 against 21.8 for Marine Components.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K Item 1 Sales, Marketing and Distribution
business_model.claim: Most component sales go directly to large OEM customers. Security Products also sells through a locksmith and OEM-distributor network, including a standardized STOCK LOCKS line.
quotes: A majority of our component sales are direct to large OEM customers
a substantial portion of our Security Products sales are made through distributors

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A; the mechanism is inferred from the risk-factor text
business_model.claim: Revenue is concentrated in a few customers and rests on purchase orders rather than long-term contracts. In 2025 the United States Postal Service was 26% of net sales and the ten largest customers were about 52%.
quotes: We sell to a diverse customer base with only one customer representing 10% or more of our consolidated net sales in 2025 (United States Postal Service representing 26%).

Because our customers’ purchases are made through purchase orders rather than long-term contracts or minimum purchase commitments, order levels can fluctuate significantly from period to period based on customer needs.

business_model.claim: Sales growth in 2025 came largely from the government security market at Security Products, which was $9.9 million higher. Marine Components rose with towboat, government and industrial sales.

including a one-time stocking event for a towboat OEM customer

accounted for approximately 14% of our total cost of sales for 2025

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K Item 7 and 10-Q figures; the operating-leverage link is inferred from the filings' own explanation

increased coverage of fixed costs due to higher sales across both segments
